**Answer** | Year | Studio Ghibli film | Japan Academy Film Prize | |------|--------------------|---------------------------| | **2002** | *Spirited Away* (released 2001) | First G‑Studio picture ever taken home the coveted “Picture of the Year” trophy | > *Spirited Away* earned the Japan Academy Film Prize for Picture of the Year during the 25th annual ceremony held in March 2002. > Prior to that, Ghibli titles were only eligible for the animation‑specific categories—“Animation Film of the Year,” “Best Screenplay,” etc.—but never topped the overall field of Japanese cinema. --- ### How the box‑office triumph amplified Ghibli’s global standing | Domestic performance | Global ripple effects | |-----------------------|------------------------| | • Grossed ¥1.18 billion (≈ US$11 million) in Japan within two months.
• Became the highest‑grossing Japanese feature of 2001.| • The record‑breaking ticket sales proved that a fully animated feature could command blockbuster status in Japan, giving producers confidence to invest larger budgets in subsequent projects. | | • Earned roughly $300 M worldwide when released in North America, Latin America, Asia, and Europe.| • The staggering revenue figures convinced foreign distributors (e.g., Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures, GKIDS, Netflix) to acquire wide theatrical and streaming rights, ensuring simultaneous multi‑region launches. | | • Garnered > 20 million admissions nationwide—a rare feat for an animated movie.| • Critics praised the film’s artistry and storytelling, earning it nominations at the Oscars, BAFTAs, and other international festivals. These accolades translated into heightened curiosity and demand outside Japan. | | • Secured the “Picture of the Year” accolade, cementing its place alongside live‑action blockbusters.| • The prestige associated with the Japan Academy Prize made Ghibli a household name even before subtitles appeared on screens abroad. Marketing campaigns leveraged the award to position the film as both culturally authentic and universally appealing. | #### Key takeaways 1. **Domestic validation → international trust:** Winning the country’s most respected cinematic award demonstrated that Ghibli’s creative vision resonated beyond niche audiences, encouraging Hollywood studios to partner on co‑distribution deals. 2. **Box‑office proof → bigger budgets & risk tolerance:** With proven profitability, Hayao Miyazaki and Toshio Suzuki secured higher production values for later features (*Ponyo*, *When Marnie Was There*, *Your Name*), allowing them to experiment with new techniques while still maintaining commercial viability. 3. **Award buzz → marketing leverage:** Promotional materials worldwide highlighted the “Japan Academy Picture of the Year” label, positioning *Spirited Away* as a premium cultural export rather than just another cartoon, thereby attracting adult viewers who might otherwise overlook anime. In short, *Spirited Away*’s dual achievement—domestic box‑office dominance coupled with the nation’s top film honour—served as a launchpad that catapulted Studio Ghibli onto the world stage, turning what began as a beloved Japanese fantasy into a global phenomenon.
